# Chapala Theological Seminary

> A free online seminary in English, Spanish, and French. Self-study Bible and theology courses, at no cost, at the student's own pace. A ministry of Common Ground Fellowship at Little Chapel, Ajijic, Jalisco, Mexico. Not accredited.

Chapala Theological Seminary (Spanish: Seminario Teológico de Chapala) offers 65 self-study courses in Bible, theology, preaching, pastoral ministry, counseling, and missions. Lessons are in English (NKJV), Spanish (RVG), and French (Louis Segond 1910). Seven foundation courses unlock the rest of the catalog.

Courses combine into four internal ministry tracks — not official academic degrees:

- Certificate of Ministry: 12 courses, including the seven foundation courses
- Associate of Divinity: 25 courses, including the seven foundation courses
- Master of Theology (Th.M.): 15 courses, including the seven foundation courses, on a master's track
- Master of Divinity (M.Div.): 30 courses, including a 20-course core, on a master's track

Each finished course can issue a class certificate. Honors is available through the Supplemental Reading Room. The seminary is non-denominational evangelical. It is **not accredited** and does not grant official Mexican degrees (Mexico requires SEP / RVOE for those). It is pursuing formal recognition in Mexico.

Director: Dr. Ted Rogers (Ph.D.). Course author: Dr. Wayne Cook (Th.D., New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary). Built for pastors and lay leaders who lack seminary access (including Cuba, Mexico, and Latin America); open to anyone.

Progress is stored in the browser and under a private student code. The code is not a public number and must never appear in a URL.

## Cómo empezar (español)

El Seminario Teológico de Chapala es un seminario en línea **gratuito** y **no acreditado**, en español, inglés y francés. Hay 65 cursos de autoestudio. Empiece por uno de los siete cursos de fundamento, regístrese una vez y guarde su código de estudiante en privado. Los títulos (Certificado de Ministerio, Asociado en Divinidad, Th.M., M.Div.) son reconocimientos internos de ministerio, no grados oficiales.
